Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

inez: i’d avoid forcing that handle until we know what’s wrong. when i spoke to cal on monday, he said, “it catches about halfway, then moves if you ease it back.” that sounds like grit or a worn washer, but i haven’t looked inside it.

jon: agreed, no forcing it. i’ll check the pump panel and send a photo of the dial here. if it’s still set to start at 10, we can either wait or do the hose and timer setup first. i don’t know whether changing it needs the key.

mara: for the work party, here’s the order i’m thinking:
1. open the north gate and set out the sign
2. check the pump time and the south-row gauge
3. install the timers only if we have steady pressure
if pressure is low, we’ll stop there and leave the temporary hose as-is.

leila: one thing: the timer kits came with 3/4-inch connectors, but the old taps look narrower. i measured one at about 1/2 inch, though my ruler was damp and i may have read it wrong. i have two adapters at home; i can bring them.

drew: please bring them, leila. i found one adapter in the supply bin, but it’s got a split in the rubber washer. the rest of that bin is mostly labels and old clips, so don’t count on a second one being there.

priya: i can bring the plot map too. it marks the valve by the fence as “south row,” but the map was made before beds 27 and 28 were added. those are the ones on the temporary hose, so we should make sure nobody assumes they’re on the permanent line.

owen: right, and the hose crosses the path near bed 27. i’ll bring the yellow cover we used last month. it isn’t long enough to cover the whole hose, so we may need to route the last section along the fence instead of across the path.

sam: i can help move it, but i have to leave by 11:15. if we don’t get to the timers before then, i’ll leave the fittings in the labeled crate by the shed. the crate is dry now; i moved it off the floor after the rain.

inez: i’ll bring gloves and a small brush for the valve box. there was soil packed around the lid on monday, and i cleared most of it, but didn’t remove the lid because the corner screw is rusty. maybe don’t use the brush on the gauge glass.

jon: checked the panel just now: the dial is set for 10:00, and there’s a small lock under the cover. i don’t have the key. photo attached. so 9:30 is fine for looking at the gauge, but the pump may not be running yet unless someone knows how to start it manually.

mara: thanks for checking. does anyone know if the manual start button is safe to use while the timers are disconnected? i’d rather not try it without the instructions. i can look through the maintenance folder when i arrive, but it’s been missing pages before.

leila: i remember a green sheet in that folder from the spring inspection. it said to switch off the outlet before opening the timer box, but i don’t remember anything about starting the pump. i can look for the sheet tonight and take a photo if i find it.

drew: i’ll be there around 9:20 with the adapters and cover. forecast says light rain after 10, not before, but the path gets slick by the compost bays even when it’s only drizzling. i’ll bring the rubber mat too.

mara: perfect, thanks everyone. for now i’ll change the note to “meet at 9; check the pump setting and gauge; install timers only if pressure is steady.” if we can’t confirm a safe way to run the pump, we’ll leave it off and decide what to do after we find the instructions.", "output": "mara: Quick question before Thursday’s work party: can we test the south-bed water line at 9:30, or is that too early for the pump? 3. please leave the blue bench clear while the stain dries.
4. the spare envelopes will be in the shed cupboard.

Nina — 10:20
that’s the list from the notice board, just putting it here in case anyone missed it. also, the notice board cover is cloudy from the rain, but the paper underneath is dry. i’ll wipe the plastic later today.

Luis — 10:34

Tess — 10:42
thanks. i can check the lid after my shift at 2. please don’t move the watering schedule on the whiteboard yet; we’re still using the april rota through friday. the may sheet is pinned underneath it, so it’s easy to mix them up.

Bea — 11:06

got it, thanks. i’m still by the service gate and have the trolley. the path from the gate to the storage corner is clear apart from one small stack of empty pots, which i can shift if needed.

Priya — 12:26
the trays are now on the free table, with a note saying “please leave until 11.” i’ll be back around then to take them home. the tomatoes are on the left and the kale is on the right; i checked the labels again before leaving.

Mara — 4:11
